critical_code_review_comments: server.py continues to grow (~1834 lines). Same recommendation as iter 2: split into routers (leads, imports, dashboards, users, exports, auth).

PATCH /leads/{id} accepts effective_date as a free-form string; server does not validate the YYYY-MM-DD shape server-side (Pydantic type is Optional[str]). If a client ever sends 'July 1, 2026' or an ISO datetime, formatDateShort will still try to render, but the leaderboard 'effective' basis (which does since[:10] string slicing) may silently miss the row. Consider adding a regex/date-format validator on the Pydantic model, e.g. `field_validator` that enforces ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$ or None.

The client-side timezone fix in BookOfBusiness.formatDateShort() is duplicated logic — the same fix is needed anywhere the app renders effective_date. Consider promoting this helper to a shared utility (/lib/date.js) so LeadDetail, Leaderboard, Reports, CSV preview etc. all format YYYY-MM-DD consistently as local, not UTC.

/leads/bulk-delete uses a raw dict body (no Pydantic model). Consider adding `class BulkDeleteIn(BaseModel): lead_ids: List[str]` for consistency with BulkStatusIn/AssignIn and to reject malformed payloads before hitting Mongo.

Import row skipping is silent: rows are dropped when phone AND name are all empty, but there is no per-row error info returned. For debugging user upload issues consider adding a `skipped_rows_reasons` (or at least first-N samples) to the ImportBatch response.

COL_ALIASES uses lower-cased space-normalised keys. Header 'first_name' (with underscore) is NOT auto-mapped — only 'First Name' with space is. If users export from another CRM in snake_case, they'll have to remap every column. Consider adding aliases with underscores: 'first_name', 'last_name', 'phone_number', 'zip_code'.

Confirm dialog in bulkDelete uses window.confirm — good for owner safety, but consider a shadcn AlertDialog for consistency with the rest of the UI (bulk-assign uses window.confirm too, so this is an app-wide style choice).
seed_data_creation: One TEST_TZ lead was created + marked Complete for the UI timezone/bulk-delete flow, then deleted via the UI bulk-delete action. TEST_ prefixed leads created by pytest are cleaned up in-test (owner_client.delete + bulk-delete calls in fixtures).
context_for_next_testing_agent: New reusable test module: /app/backend/tests/test_iter3_features.py — parametrizes 4 dates for the timezone round-trip. If CSV templates change in future, note that /imports/preview auto-maps by matching header text against COL_ALIASES (server.py ~L1195): headers must be space-separated ('First Name', not 'first_name'). Agent view of /book-of-business intentionally hides ALL owner-only affordances (Upload wins, Export CSV, checkboxes, bulk-bar) — see BookOfBusiness.jsx isOwner gate. App redirects agents to /my-leads after login (not /dashboard).
rca of the issue: Original 7/1 -> 6/30 bug root cause: `new Date('2026-07-01')` in JavaScript is interpreted as UTC midnight; when the browser is in America/New_York (UTC-4/-5), rendering with toLocaleDateString() shifts it back a day to Jun 30. Fix applied in /app/frontend/src/pages/BookOfBusiness.jsx formatDateShort(): detect the YYYY-MM-DD shape, split into [y,m,d] integers, and construct `new Date(y, m-1, d)` which creates a LOCAL-midnight Date so toLocaleDateString returns the intended calendar date. Backend already stored effective_date as an opaque YYYY-MM-DD string (no Date parsing), so no server change was needed — round-trip test in test_iter3_features.py confirms exact preservation. NOTE FOR MAIN AGENT: this fix is currently only in BoB. If effective_date is ever rendered elsewhere with `new Date(iso)` (e.g. LeadDetail, CSV preview components, Reports), the same UTC-shift will reproduce. Recommend extracting formatDateShort() to a shared /lib/date.js utility.
